hints: Look carefully at where each arrow sits on the circle. V is on the G1 to S boundary and W is on the S to G2 boundary, so ask yourself which one has just finished S phase.
Remember what G2 is for. DNA is already doubled in S, then G2 grows the cell and makes tubulin and new centrioles for the spindle before prophase condenses the chromosomes.
walkthrough:
**Map V, W, X and Y onto the cycle**

Great start, let us read the circle clockwise. V is at the end of G1 and start of S. W is at the end of S and start of G2. X is at the end of G2 and start of mitosis. Y is at the end of mitosis and start of cytokinesis.

**Find DNA replication complete but still growing**

DNA replication happens in S phase, so it is complete just as S ends. Maximum size is reached at the end of G2, after growth and protein synthesis. So we want early G2, just after S. That is cell W.

**Find spindle preparation almost done but no condensation yet**

In G2 the cell makes tubulin proteins and duplicates centrioles to prepare microtubules for the spindle. Chromosome condensation does not happen until prophase of mitosis. So we want late G2, just before mitosis. That is cell X.

Together that gives W and X, which is row D.

options.A: V is at the G1 to S boundary, so DNA replication has not even started, and X alone is correct for the second column.
options.B: W is correct for the first column, but Y is in mitosis to cytokinesis when chromosomes are already condensed and the spindle is already formed.
options.C: Both are wrong. V has not replicated DNA yet, and Y has already passed chromosome condensation in mitosis.
options.D: W is early G2 after S has finished DNA replication but before G2 growth is complete, and X is late G2 with spindle preparation nearly done but before prophase condensation.
